source_text:
Gal 2,18 Πρὸς τὸν Πέτρον ὁ λόγος· σὺ κατέλυσας αὐτὰ δόγματι ὅπερ ἀπεστάλη παρ' ὑμῶν τοῖς
Ἀντιοχεῦσι καὶ πάσῃ τῇ οἰκουμένῃ. ἀπρεπὲς οὖν ταύτα διδάσκειν ἑτέρους, ὧν τῆς ἐπιμελείας ἀπέστης καὶ ἰδίῳ κατέλυσας δόγματι. Gal 2,19– Ὁ νόμος τῶν σωματικῶν ἔχει τὴν ἐργασίαν καὶ τὴν ἀπόλαυσιν, τόδε φάγε καὶ τόδε μὴ φάγῃς, σάββατον τήρησον, περιτομήν. ἡ χάρις οὐ βούλεταί σε διὰ τούτων εὐδοκιμεῖν. ἐνεκρώθην οὖν, φησί, τούτοις. τί χρείαν ἔχω νόμου; Ζῶ δὲ οὐκέτι ἐγώ, ζῇ δὲ ἐν ἐμοὶ Χριστός. ὃ ἐγὼ ἔζων ἐμαυτῷ, ὑπὸ νόμον ἤμην. ἐπειδὴ δὲ Χριστὸς ζῇ ἐν ἐμοί, ὁ μηκέτι ὑπὸ νόμον ἀλλ' ἐν οὐρανοῖς ἐκ δεξιῶν τοῦ πατρός, οὐκ ἀθετῶ τὸν ἐν ἐμοὶ ζῶντα. Ὃ δὲ νῦν ζῶ ἐν σαρκί, ἐν πίστει ζῶ. πιστεύω γὰρ εἰς τὸν υἱὸν τοῦ θεοῦ. εἰ δὲ ὁ υἱὸς τοῦ θεοῦ ᾧ πιστεύω, ἐν δεξιᾷ τοῦ πατρός, ἐν οὐρανοῖς πολιτεύομαι· ὁ δὲ νόμος ἐν τοῖς ἐπὶ γῆς εἶχε τὰς τηρήσεις. οὐκ ἄρα ὑπόκειμαι νόμῳ. 301 Gal 3,19–22 Ἐβάρει πλέον ὁ νόμος, καὶ διακονία θανάτου διὰ τοῦτο ὠνόμασται. πῶς οὖν τῶν παραβάσεων χάριν προσετέθη, φησίν; ἐν συντόμῳ ῥήματι τοιοῦτόν ἐστιν· πρὸ νόμου καὶ ὁ νοῦς τῶν ἀνθρώπων μετὰ τῆς σαρκὸς ἐδούλευσε τῇ ἁμαρτίᾳ καὶ ἔστεργε τὸ κακόν, δοθέντος τοῦ νόμου ὁ μὲν νοῦς ἐπαιδεύθη, ἡ δὲ σὰρξ ἔτι κατείχετο. ἐπεὶ οὖν ὁ μὲν ἀγνοῶν τὴν ἁμαρτίαν ὅτι ἁμαρτία ἦν, τὴν ἀσέβειαν ὡς εὐσέβειαν μετιὼν καὶ σπουδαιότερον αὐτῇ προσέχει, ὁ δὲ γνοὺς ὅτι κακόν, τοῦτο γοῦν κερδανεῖ τὸ συνειδέναι ὅτι παραβαίνει, καὶ ἐπιθυμεῖ τῷ θεῷ ὑπακοῦσαι. διὰ τοῦτο ἐδόθη νόμος ὁ δυνάμενος ζωοποιῆσαι, ἀντὶ τοῦ εἰ ἐδόθη νόμος, οὐκ ἐδόθη, φησί, κατὰ τῶν ἐπαγγελιῶν τοῦ θεοῦ, ἀλλ' οὐδὲ διὰ παντὸς κρατεῖν ἐδύνατο. Gal 3,23 Εἰ καὶ μηδὲν ἕτερον κατώρθου ὁ νόμος, ἀλλὰ τὸ τὸν θεὸν εἰδέναι παρεῖχεν. τὸ δὲ τὸν θεὸν εἰδέναι ἕτοιμον ἐποίει πρὸς τὴν τῆς χάριτος ὑποδοχήν. Gal 3,27–28 Οὐχ ἡ τοῦ νόμου τήρησις, φησί, βελτίονας ποιεῖ τοὺς πιστεύσαντας τῶν ἀπὸ τῶν ἐθνῶν τοὺς Ἰουδαίους, ἀλλ' ἡ δύναμις τοῦ βαπτίσματος τὸ Χριστὸν ἐνδύσασθαι παρέχουσα, κοινὴν ποιεῖ τὴν χάριν πάντων ὁμοῦ, βαρβάρων, Ἑλλήνων, Ἰουδαίων, θήλεος, ἄρρενος. οὐχ ἁπλῶς δὲ παρέμιξε τὸ θῆλυ καὶ τὸ ἄρρεν–ὅσον γὰρ εἷς τῷ ῥήματι ἐζήτει πρὸς τὸ προκείμενον–, ἀλλ' εἰ τὸ ἄρρεν καὶ τὸ θῆλυ διαφέρον εἰς μίαν χάριν συνάγει τὸ βάπτισμα, πόσῳ μᾶλλον Ἕλληνα καὶ Ἰουδαῖον. Gal 4,8–10 Νῦν βούλεται δεῖξαι ὅτι μετὰ τὸ τὴν χάριν ἐλθεῖν, κἂν δοκῇ τις κατὰ νόμον σάββατον τηρεῖν καὶ νεομηνίας καὶ ἑορτάς, ὥσπερ εἰδωλολατρεῖ τοῖς στοιχείοις οἷς ἐθρήσκευεν ἐθνικὸς ὤν, ἄλλως δουλεύων.
thought_title: The law's bodily works are dead; baptism clothes all with Christ
orientation: Eusebius is commenting on Paul's words to Peter at Antioch and then on Galatians 2:18–4:10, explaining why the law's bodily observances are dead for the believer and why baptism makes grace common to all.
pass_a_gloss: Gal 2:18 Toward Peter the word [is]: you destroyed them by a decree which was sent from you to the Antiochenes and to all the inhabited world. Unseemly therefore [it is] to teach these things to others, from whose care you withdrew and by your own decree you destroyed [it]. Gal 2:19– The law of the bodily things has the working and the enjoyment, this eat and this do not eat, keep Sabbath, circumcision. The grace does not wish you to be approved through these things. I was made dead therefore, he says, to these things. What need do I have of the law? And I no longer live, but Christ lives in me. What I was living for myself, I was under the law. But since Christ lives in me, who [is] no longer under the law but in the heavens at the right hand of the Father, I do not reject the one living in me. But what I now live in the flesh, in faith I live. For I believe in the Son of God. But if the Son of God in whom I believe [is] at the right hand of the Father, in the heavens I have my citizenship; but the law among the things on earth had the observances. Not therefore I am subject to the law. 301 Gal 3:19–22 The law weighed more heavily, and a ministry of death because of this it has been named. How therefore for the sake of transgressions was it added, he says? In a brief word such is [the answer]: before the law also the mind of humans with the flesh served sin and loved the evil; when the law was given, the mind was trained, but the flesh still was held down. Since therefore the one not knowing sin that it was sin, pursuing impiety as piety and more zealously attending to it, but the one knowing that [it is] evil, this at least he will gain, to know that he transgresses, and he desires to obey God. Because of this a law was given that could give life, instead of if a law was given, it was not given, he says, against the promises of God, but neither was it able to rule forever. Gal 3:23 Even if nothing else the law accomplished, but it provided knowing God. But knowing God made [one] ready for the reception of grace. Gal 3:27–28 Not the observance of the law, he says, makes the Jews who believed better than those from the nations, but the power of baptism providing putting on Christ makes common the grace of all together, barbarians, Greeks, Jews, female, male. Not simply did he mix the female and the male—for as much as one in the word was seeking toward the matter at hand—, but if the male and the female differing into one grace baptism brings together, how much more Greek and Jew. Gal 4:8–10 Now he wishes to show that after grace came, even if someone seems according to the law to keep Sabbath and new moons and feasts, just as he commits idolatry to the basic principles which he worshipped being a Gentile, otherwise serving.

choices.why: Keeps the moral impropriety of teaching what one has abandoned, without modernizing to 'inappropriate' or 'wrong'.

choices.english: I was made dead to these things
choices.why: Preserves the passive voice and the dative of relation, matching Paul's 'I died to the law' language.
Captures the civic metaphor of heavenly citizenship that Eusebius develops later in the fragment.
Keeps the comparative force of πλέον and the metaphor of weight, which leads into 'ministry of death'.
Standard rendering for the clothing metaphor of baptism in Galatians 3:27, kept literal.
Follows the glossary vote for στοιχεῖα, avoiding 'elemental spirits' which would over-interpret the cosmology.

pass_b_english: The word is addressed to Peter: you destroyed them by a decree which had been sent from you to Antioch and to the whole world. It is unseemly, then, to teach others what you abandoned and destroyed by your own decree.

The law has its work and its enjoyment in bodily things: eat this, do not eat that, keep the Sabbath, circumcision. Grace does not want to win approval through these things. So I was made dead to these things, he says. What need do I have of the law? I no longer live, but Christ lives in me. The life I lived for myself—that was under the law. But since Christ lives in me—who is no longer under the law but in heaven at the right hand of the Father—I do not reject the one living in me. And what I now live in the flesh, I live in faith. For I believe in the Son of God. And if the Son of God in whom I believe is at the right hand of the Father, I have my citizenship in heaven; but the law had its observances among things on earth. Therefore I am not subject to the law.

The law weighed more heavily, and for this reason it was named a ministry of death. How then was it added because of transgressions, he says? In a brief word, it is this: before the law, the mind of human beings along with the flesh was enslaved to sin and loved evil; when the law was given, the mind was trained, but the flesh was still held down. Since, then, the one who does not know that sin is sin pursues impiety as piety and attends to it more eagerly, while the one who knows that it is evil gains at least this: the awareness that he is transgressing, and he desires to obey God. For this reason a law able to give life—meaning that if a law was given, it was not given, he says, against the promises of God, but neither could it have power forever.
Even if the law accomplished nothing else, it provided the knowledge of God. And the knowledge of God made one ready to receive grace.

It is not the observance of the law, he says, that makes the Jews who believe better than those from the nations, but the power of baptism, which provides the putting on of Christ, makes grace common to all together—barbarians, Greeks, Jews, female, male. He did not simply mix in female and male—as far as one sought in one phrase for the matter at hand—but if baptism brings male and female, though different, into one grace, how much more Greek and Jew.

Now he wants to show that after grace has come, even if someone seems to keep the Sabbath according to the law, and new moons and festivals, he is as one committing idolatry to the basic principles he worshiped when he was a Gentile, serving them in another way.

problems.why: ὃ is 'the life which,' not 'what'; relative pronoun referring to life, not general 'what.'
problems.fix: The life I lived for myself

problems.quote: a law was given that could give life
problems.why: Misreads syntax: this is Eusebius's compressed explanation, not 'a law that could give life' as if positive; it's concessive 'though able to give life.'
problems.fix: a law, though able to give life—instead of saying, if a law had been given, it was not given, he says, against God's promises

problems.quote: he commits idolatry to the basic principles
problems.why: ὥσπερ means 'as if/as though,' not simple 'he commits'; it's comparative, showing resemblance to idolatry.
problems.fix: he is as one committing idolatry to the basic principles
problems.ruling: ὥσπερ 'just as' is comparative; English drops the comparison, making idolatry direct not analogous.

edits.new: The life I lived for myself

edits.old: a law was given that could give life—instead of saying, if a law had been given, it was not given, he says, against the promises of God
edits.new: a law, though able to give life—instead of saying, if a law had been given, it was not given, he says, against the promises of God

edits.old: he commits idolatry to the basic principles
edits.new: he is as one committing idolatry to the basic principles

fixed: Corrected 'What I lived for myself' to 'The life I lived for myself' to reflect the relative pronoun ὃ referring to life.
Corrected 'a law was given that could give life' to 'a law, though able to give life' to reflect the concessive syntax.
Corrected 'he commits idolatry' to 'he is as one committing idolatry' to reflect the comparative ὥσπερ.

problems.quote: you destroyed these things by the decree that was sent from you
problems.source_quote: σὺ κατέλυσας αὐτὰ δόγματι ὅπερ ἀπεστάλη παρ' ὑμῶν
problems.why: Agency reversed: Peter destroyed the decree, not destroyed things by the decree.
problems.fix: you destroyed them by a decree, though one had been sent from you

problems.quote: The life I lived for myself, I was under the law
problems.source_quote: ὃ ἐγὼ ἔζων ἐμαυτῷ, ὑπὸ νόμον ἤμην
problems.why: Missing connection: two clauses are juxtaposed as cause and effect, not just listed.
problems.fix: The life I lived for myself—that was under the law

problems.quote: a law, though able to give life—instead of saying, if a law had been given, it was not given
problems.source_quote: ὁ δυνάμενος ζωοποιῆσαι, ἀντὶ τοῦ εἰ ἐδόθη νόμος, οὐκ ἐδόθη
problems.why: Garbled syntax: 'instead of saying' misrepresents ἀντὶ τοῦ, which introduces Paul's compressed argument.
problems.fix: a law able to give life—meaning, if a law had been given, it was not given

problems.quote: as far as the word required for the matter at hand
problems.source_quote: ὅσον γὰρ εἷς τῷ ῥήματι ἐζήτει πρὸς τὸ προκείμενον
problems.why: Wrong subject: 'the word' for ῥήματι obscures that 'one' (a person) sought in speech.
problems.fix: as far as one sought in the argument for the matter at hand
problems.ruling: εἷς τῷ ῥήματι ἐζήτει = 'one sought by word'; English 'the word required' loses personal subject εἷς.

edits.old: you destroyed these things by the decree that was sent from you
edits.new: you destroyed them by a decree, though one had been sent from you

edits.old: The life I lived for myself, I was under the law.
edits.new: The life I lived for myself—that was under the law.

edits.old: a law, though able to give life—instead of saying, if a law had been given, it was not given
edits.new: a law able to give life—meaning, if a law had been given, it was not given

edits.old: as far as the word required for the matter at hand

fixed: All four confirmed problems required edits and have been addressed.

problems.quote: you destroyed them by a decree, though one had been sent from you
problems.source_quote: σὺ κατέλυσας αὐτὰ δόγματι ὅπερ ἀπεστάλη παρ' ὑμῶν
problems.why: ὅπερ is 'which,' not 'though one'; Peter destroyed the very decree sent from them.
problems.fix: you destroyed them by a decree which had been sent from you

problems.quote: what you have stopped caring for
problems.why: ἀπέστης means 'you abandoned/desisted from,' not 'stopped caring for'—stronger renunciation.
problems.fix: what you abandoned and destroyed by your own decree

problems.quote: a law able to give life—meaning, if a law had been given, it was not given
problems.source_quote: ὁ δυνάμενος ζωοποιῆσαι, ἀντὶ τοῦ εἰ ἐδόθη νόμος, οὐκ ἐδόθη
problems.why: ἀντὶ τοῦ = 'instead of/meaning that if a law had been given, it was not given'—the 'meaning' construction is garbled; this explains why the life-giving law was NOT given against promises.
problems.fix: a law able to give life—meaning that if a law had been given, it was not given

problems.quote: Grace does not want you to win approval through these things
problems.source_quote: ἡ χάρις οὐ βούλεταί σε διὰ τούτων εὐδοκιμεῖν
problems.why: σε is accusative subject of infinitive: 'grace does not want to win approval through these'—no 'you'.
problems.fix: Grace does not want to win approval through these things
problems.ruling: σε is accusative subject of εὐδοκιμεῖν: 'grace does not want you to win approval' is correct, not 'grace does not want to win approval.'

problems.quote: as far as one sought in the argument for the matter at hand
problems.source_quote: ὅσον γὰρ εἷς τῷ ῥήματι ἐζήτει πρὸς τὸ προκείμενον
problems.why: εἷς τῷ ῥήματι = 'in one word/phrase,' not 'in the argument'; he didn't mix them in merely for brevity's sake.
problems.fix: as far as one sought in one phrase for the matter at hand
problems.ruling: εἷς τῷ ῥήματι = 'in one word/phrase'; 'in the argument' mistranslates εἷς and ῥήματι, changing meaning.
